findings.state: reload, back-forward, observer disconnect, and conflicting session/evidence routing
findings.visibleEvidence: The source-bound observe-step07 mobile event trace records only context setup, synthetic completed storage, one canonical adult-tool route open, and capture. Across the supplied agent trace archives there are no page.reload, page.goBack, page.goForward, history navigation, or disconnect action records. The 40-row deep matrix covers canonical Step 06 and Step 07 routes but contains no invalid or conflicting evidence/session URL row.
findings.whyItMatters: Without executable lifecycle and conflict evidence, a regression could lose or duplicate progress on refresh/history traversal, misclassify Step 07 as Step 06 when parameters conflict, or leave the adult observer in a misleading connected state after the child window closes while every current canonical-open row still passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add source-bound isolated Playwright adversarial cases that perform reload, back, forward, child-window close/disconnect, and Step06/Step07/bare-session conflict URLs. Assert exact observation context or fail-closed denial, storage continuity, observer connection state, zero external requests, and capture screenshot, ARIA, and trace/event evidence for each case.

findings.state: structure placement and state-transition controls under burst input
findings.visibleEvidence: HESITANT_WITH_HINTS explicitly demonstrates two reversible invalid placements and eventual completion, while the deep placing row captures a valid static placement state. Neither the profile interactions nor the supplied trace inventory declares rapid double-click, repeated Enter/Space, multi-touch burst, or overlapping drag/tap actuation against a transition control.
findings.whyItMatters: Single-step correctness does not prove transition idempotence. A young child can tap or press repeatedly, which may double-advance a scene, consume the wrong card, apply progress twice, or create a save state that normal paced interactions never reach.
findings.suggestedFix: Add deterministic burst-input cases at card selection, slot placement, ability choice, boss completion, finish-run, and return-world controls. Verify one logical transition, one save update, reversible invalid feedback, and no console/page errors, then preserve screenshot, ARIA, and Playwright trace evidence.

findings.visibleEvidence: The accepted classic-hub ARIA candidate has a top-level main landmark containing navigation, the level-one heading, filters, and then a second main landmark wrapping the ten game cards. The deep row reports focus and target checks as PASS, but those checks do not reject nested main landmarks.
findings.whyItMatters: Nested main landmarks are invalid document structure and can make landmark navigation ambiguous for keyboard and screen-reader users even when every button remains individually focusable.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep exactly one main landmark for the page, change the inner catalog container to a named section or div, and add a semantic assertion that each route exposes exactly one non-nested main landmark before establishing the ARIA baseline.

limitations: This is machine-only QA over synthetic isolated browser contexts; it does not establish real-child behavior, fun, comfort, learning, retention, preference, or long-term engagement.

The supplied raw package contains no explicit reload, back-forward, observer-disconnect, conflicting-route, or burst-input trace, so those behaviors are recorded as unverified rather than inferred PASS.
The ten classic games were reviewed smoke-only; no deep gameplay or learning-quality conclusion is made for them.
